subject: mathematics
title: Negative Numbers & Shifts on the Number Line
summary: Negative numbers represent values less than zero, such as sub-zero temperatures, underground floors, or depths below sea level.
visualInteractiveHint: Pick the starting point and shift on the number line: adding moves right (+) and subtracting moves left (−).
workedExampleTitle: Walking the number line: start at −4 and add +7

workedSteps.title: Step 1: Locate the starting position
workedSteps.explanation: −4 sits 4 steps to the left of 0.

workedSteps.title: Step 2: Step back to zero first
workedSteps.explanation: Out of the 7 steps to the right, the first 4 steps bring us from −4 right up to 0.

workedSteps.title: Step 3: Take the remaining steps past zero
workedSteps.explanation: Since we needed to move 7 steps and used 4, we move 3 more steps to the right of 0, landing on +3.

whyItWorks: Every negative number is the mirror opposite of its positive twin across 0. That is why −4 and +4 cancel out to 0.

commonMistake.wrongExample: Common trap: thinking −8 is greater than −2 because 8 is greater than 2.
commonMistake.correction: On the number line, numbers further to the right are always greater. −2 °C is warmer (greater) than −8 °C.

deepDiveExtra: Subtracting a negative number, like 5 − (−3), removes a debt of 3: it shifts you right, so 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8.

quickChecks.question: If you start at −3 and move 4 steps further left (−3 − 4), where do you land?
quickChecks.explanation: Start 3 units left of 0 and move 4 more units left: you reach −7.

quickChecks.question: Which temperature is higher (greater)?
quickChecks.explanation: −2 is further to the right on the number line (closer to 0) than −9.
